concepts.title: Classifying Alcohols by Hydroxyl Count and Carbon Type
concepts.definition: Alcohols group as mono-, di-, tri- or polyhydric by how many hydroxyl groups each molecule carries, and monohydric ones split further by the carbon bearing the -OH: primary, secondary or tertiary in a plain chain, allylic or benzylic when that sp3 carbon sits beside a double bond or ring, and vinylic when the carbon itself is sp2.
concepts.key_idea: Ethers mirror this logic on oxygen: identical groups give symmetrical ethers, different groups give mixed ones.
question_patterns: classify the isomeric alcohols of C5H12O as primary, secondary or tertiary
label CH2=CHCH2OH as an allylic, benzylic or vinylic alcohol

solution_steps.explain: one, two, three or many OH groups tag the alcohol mono-, di-, tri- or polyhydric
count its carbon neighbours for 1/2/3 degree, then check for an adjacent C=C or ring (allylic, benzylic) or sp2 character (vinylic)

concepts.title: IUPAC Naming of Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers
concepts.definition: Alcohol names swap the alkane ending -e for -ol, numbered from the end nearest the hydroxyl group, with di- and tri- marks for several OH groups; ethers are named as alkoxy substituents on the larger hydrocarbon parent, while phenol derivatives use 1,2-, 1,3- and 1,4- locants.
concepts.key_idea: For cyclic alcohols the OH carbon counts as C-1, and the bigger group is always the parent in an ether name.

solution_steps.action: choose the parent for each family
solution_steps.explain: alcohols use the longest chain with the OH carbon; ethers promote the larger group to parent with an alkoxy prefix

solution_steps.action: number for the lowest OH locants
solution_steps.explain: the hydroxyl carbon takes the smallest possible number before other substituents are placed

concepts.title: Alcohols from Alkenes: Markovnikov Hydration versus Hydroboration
concepts.definition: Water adds across a double bond in acid via a carbocation, so the OH lands on the more substituted carbon (Markovnikov); hydroboration-oxidation instead parks boron on the less substituted end and hands over the anti-Markovnikov alcohol in excellent yield.
concepts.key_idea: Hydration runs protonation, water attack, then deprotonation; hydroboration avoids rearrangements because no free carbocation ever forms.
concepts.textbook_ref: lech202.txt section 7.4.1(1) with mechanism and H.C. Brown box (lines ~503-584)

solution_steps.explain: acid plus water follows Markovnikov through a carbocation; BH3 then H2O2/OH- delivers the opposite orientation
Markovnikov puts OH on the carbon with fewer hydrogens; hydroboration puts it on the carbon with more

concepts.title: Alcohols from Carbonyl Compounds and Grignard Reagents
concepts.definition: Hydrogen adds to the carbonyl group either catalytically or via NaBH4/LiAlH4, aldehydes giving primary alcohols and ketones secondary ones; a Grignard reagent adds first as a nucleophile and hydrolysis of the adduct then fixes the degree: methanal yields primary, any other aldehyde secondary, ketones tertiary.
concepts.key_idea: Counting the carbons that surround the carbinol carbon tells you the alcohol class before you even draw the mechanism.

solution_steps.explain: aldehyde carbons carry one carbon neighbour, ketone carbons two; reduction preserves that count

solution_steps.action: add the Grignard carbon where relevant
solution_steps.explain: the reagent's R group joins the carbonyl carbon, raising the alcohol degree by the number of carbons added

concepts.title: Four Laboratory Routes to Phenol
concepts.definition: Phenol comes from benzene derivatives four ways: fusing chlorobenzene with NaOH at 623 K and 320 atmospheres then acidifying, heating benzene sulphonic acid with molten NaOH, hydrolysing a diazonium salt with warm water, or oxidising cumene with air and splitting the hydroperoxide with dilute acid.
concepts.key_idea: The cumene process dominates world production because acetone arrives as a valuable co-product.

concepts.title: Hydrogen Bonding behind Boiling Points and Solubility
concepts.definition: Intermolecular O-H...O hydrogen bonds lift alcohol and phenol boiling points above ethers, haloalkanes and hydrocarbons of similar mass, branching weakens the effect, and the same bonding to water dissolves small alcohols freely until bulky hydrophobic groups crowd it out.
concepts.key_idea: Ethoxyethane and butan-1-ol dissolve in water to nearly the same extent because ether oxygen hydrogen-bonds to water even without an O-H of its own.
question_patterns: explain why propanol boils far higher than butane

solution_steps.action: look for donor and acceptor sites
solution_steps.explain: an O-H bond donates hydrogen bonds; a lone-pair oxygen can only accept them

concepts.title: Acidity of Alcohols and Phenols with Substituent Effects
concepts.definition: Both families donate the O-H proton to metals and strong bases, but phenol outstrips alcohol acidity because its phenoxide ion spreads the negative charge over the ring while an alkoxide keeps it stuck on oxygen; alkyl groups weaken the acid and nitro groups at ortho or para strengthen it.
concepts.key_idea: Alkoxides beat hydroxide as proton acceptors, which is exactly why sodium ethoxide outbases sodium hydroxide.
concepts.textbook_ref: lech202.txt section 7.4.4(a), Table 7.3 pKa data, Example 7.4 (lines ~773-902)
question_patterns: arrange propan-1-ol, phenol, 3-nitrophenol, 3,5-dinitrophenol, picric acid and 4-methylphenol by growing acid strength

solution_steps.explain: charge delocalisation over the ring stabilises phenoxide; alkyl groups intensify charge on oxygen and destabilise

concepts.title: Acid Strength Ratio from pKa Values
concepts.definition: Each pKa hides a base-ten factor: converting both values to Ka by raising ten to the minus pKa, then dividing, tells how many times one acid out-ionises the other.
concepts.key_idea: A pKa gap of about six units is why phenol is called a million-fold stronger acid than ethanol, and bigger pKa always means the weaker acid.

concepts.title: Alcohol-to-Halide Routes and the Lucas Test
concepts.definition: Hydrogen halides, phosphorus tribromide and thionyl chloride swap an alcohol's OH for a halogen, and the three classes differ visibly with Lucas reagent (concentrated HCl plus ZnCl2): tertiary alcohols turn cloudy at once, secondary in minutes, primary only on heating.
concepts.key_idea: Turbidity timing works because immiscible alkyl halides scatter light the instant they form, and halide reactivity runs HI > HBr > HCl.
question_patterns: how does the Lucas reagent tell a tertiary alcohol from a primary one

solution_steps.action: match the alcohol class to its carbocation stability
solution_steps.explain: the reaction price is a carbocation, so tertiary alcohols respond fastest in both halogenation and dehydration
immediate cloudiness marks tertiary, slow cloudiness secondary, and heating is needed for primary

concepts.title: Oxidation Ladder of Alcohols
concepts.definition: Primary alcohols climb to aldehydes under mild agents like PCC or CrO3 and on to carboxylic acids with strong ones like acidified KMnO4; secondary alcohols stop at ketones, tertiary alcohols resist oxidation unless bonds are torn apart, and hot copper at 573 K dehydrogenates the first two classes while dehydrating the third.
concepts.key_idea: Picking the reagent picks the rung: mild oxidation pauses at the aldehyde, strong oxidation pushes through to the acid.
concepts.textbook_ref: lech202.txt section 7.4.4(b)(4) with PCC and copper box (lines ~971-1050)

concepts.title: Ring Reactions of Phenol: Nitration, Bromination, Kolbe and Reimer-Tiemann
concepts.definition: The OH group floods the ring with electron density, so electrophiles attack ortho and para: dilute nitric acid gives a separable o- and p-nitrophenol mix, bromine water drops the white 2,4,6-tribromophenol precipitate even without a Lewis acid, phenoxide plus carbon dioxide builds salicylic acid (Kolbe), and chloroform in alkali installs an ortho CHO group (Reimer-Tiemann).
concepts.key_idea: Ortho nitrophenol steams off first because its intramolecular hydrogen bond breaks association, unlike the intermolecularly bonded para isomer.

solution_steps.action: let the OH group direct the electrophile
solution_steps.explain: resonance enriches ortho and para positions, and the phenoxide ion is reactive enough even for CO2

solution_steps.action: match the condition to the substitution depth
solution_steps.explain: low-polarity solvent keeps bromination monosubstituted; excess bromine water takes all three positions

concepts.title: Fermentation Stoichiometry of Glucose to Ethanol
concepts.definition: Zymase from yeast splits one glucose molecule into two ethanol molecules and two of carbon dioxide under anaerobic conditions, so moles of glucose in hand fix the alcohol yield twice over, and multiplying by the molar mass turns that into grams.
concepts.key_idea: Fermentation stalls near 14 percent alcohol because zymase poisons itself, and oxygen leaking in oxidises ethanol to ethanoic acid.

solution_steps.explain: each glucose splits into two ethanol molecules under zymase

concepts.title: Making Ethers: Acid Dehydration and Williamson Synthesis
concepts.definition: Two primary alcohols dehydrated by acid at about 413 K couple into a symmetrical ether through an SN2 attack on a protonated alcohol, while Williamson synthesis couples a primary alkyl halide with sodium alkoxide for symmetrical or mixed ethers; a tertiary halide instead surrenders an alkene because alkoxides are strong bases too.
concepts.key_idea: Put the bulky fragment on the oxygen side, never on the halide side: tertiary halides eliminate, they do not substitute.
question_patterns: write the Williamson route to 2-ethoxy-3-methylpentane from an alcohol and a halide

solution_steps.explain: the alkyl halide in Williamson must be primary; bulky groups belong in the alkoxide

concepts.title: Reactions of Ethers: HI Cleavage and Activated Ring Substitution
concepts.definition: Concentrated HI or HBr cuts the ether C-O bond: iodide attacks the least hindered carbon by SN2, tertiary groups leave as carbocations by SN1, and aryl-alkyl ethers always break at the alkyl side leaving phenol plus alkyl iodide; the alkoxy group meanwhile activates aromatic rings toward ortho and para substitution, anisole brominating para in about 90 percent yield.
concepts.key_idea: The aryl-oxygen bond resists cleavage thanks to partial double-bond character, so electrophilic substitution and C-O cutting happen on different halves of the molecule.
concepts.textbook_ref: lech202.txt sections 7.6.2-7.6.3 with mechanism and Example 7.7 (lines ~1362-1550)
